svg.title: SyzFlux Detailed Architecture - Kafka, Index Strategy, and Storage Tiers
svg.desc: Detailed observability architecture: unified ingest via Kafka, Streama in-stream processing without full indexing, TCO routing to OpenSearch hot index vs customer S3 Parquet cold archive, queried by DataPrime.
svg.text: How Kafka streaming, selective indexing, and S3 cold storage deliver one platform at low TCO
Source - Stream - Sink on Kafka Streams

g.text: Process events IN MOTION - before (or without) full indexing
Route at ingest - not after bloat
Ingest -> INDEX EVERYTHING hot -> pay forever
Index = inverted text + field maps + replicas
Ingest -> stream analyze -> index ONLY High
Med/Low = columnar Parquet on S3 (no ES index)
- Index often 1.5-3x raw size (tokens, docs, segments)
- Hot SSD / RAM for search clusters is costly
- Alerting waits on index refresh (latency tax)
Inverted + field indices for sub-second search
- Critical app logs and error paths
Highest $/GB - keep volume small via TCO
- No rehydrate tax - DataPrime queries remote
Med: alerting + dashboards | Low: compliance retain
Same query across hot index + S3 archive
Agents query the same unified data layer

svg.text: 8. HOW KAFKA ENABLES ONE EFFICIENT PLATFORM

g.text: and AI telemetry share one Kafka
and derive metrics while data is
still in Kafka - storage is optional.
state stores - not only in a hot DB.
Kafka = the nervous system (ingest, buffer, fan-out, in-stream compute).
Index = scarce resource applied only to High-priority data in OpenSearch.
S3 Parquet = cheap long-term body of truth, still queryable - so you keep more data for less money on one platform.
